plants.name: Euphorbia pulcherrima
plants.description: Wild poinsettias are tall, leggy shrubs. Their fiery bracts, which are leaves that look like petals, blaze in the dry season and surround tiny yellow flower clusters. The bracts are the showy part, and they light up hillsides and gardens at the start of the holiday season.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to winter, roughly November through February
plants.location: Native to southern Mexico and Central America, where it blooms in the wild. It is also grown outdoors in warm regions such as southern California and Florida.
plants.funFact: Poinsettias flower in response to long nights. They need about 12 hours or more of uninterrupted darkness each day for several weeks to set their colorful bracts. That is why they peak around the winter holidays.

plants.name: Schlumbergera truncata
plants.description: This is a forest-dwelling cactus with arching, segmented stems. In late autumn, the stem tips bear dangling, asymmetrical flowers that look like small tropical lanterns. In the wild it perches on tree branches and rocks in cool, misty mountain forests.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn into early winter, typically November through December
plants.location: Native to the coastal mountains of southeastern Brazil near Rio de Janeiro. It is widely grown as a houseplant across North America and Europe.
plants.funFact: This cactus grows on trees and has no spines. It is an epiphyte, and its flat, jointed stems have pointed teeth along the edges. Those teeth are one way to tell it apart from the Christmas cactus, which has scalloped edges.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: In late spring, this tree is covered in clouds of lavender-blue trumpet flowers. The blooms drop to carpet streets and gardens in violet. Its feathery, fern-like leaves add to the dreamy look of the canopy.
plants.bloomingSeason: Southern Hemisphere spring, from about October to December. Blooming peaks in November in many places.
plants.location: Native to South America. It is grown as a street tree in Australia, South Africa and Argentina. It flowers around December 1 in places such as Brisbane and Sydney, where the bloom is tapering off.
plants.funFact: Jacaranda trees are popular in Pretoria, South Africa, which is nicknamed the Jacaranda City. The tree is a favorite in Australia, where its bloom is linked with the end of the university year.
